title: Europe’s Ancient Landscapes May Have Been More Open Than We Thought
paragraphs: Scientists studied the past of Europe. They looked at very old plants, animals and pollen. Long ago, Europe was not one big, dark forest.
Many places had trees, but other places were open. They had grass and flowers. Big animals lived there, like elephants, rhinos and bison.
These animals ate plants and walked on the ground. This kept many places open. The scientists say people should think about this today.

questions.q: Was Europe always one big dark forest?
questions.a: No. It also had open places.
They ate plants and kept places open.
